status_summary: A DHS memorandum dated 2025-01-20 and signed by the Acting Secretary rescinded the 2021-10-27 guidelines on enforcement actions in or near protected areas such as houses of worship, schools and hospitals, and called for officer discretion in place of fixed rules. Courts have since limited the policy only for particular plaintiffs: on 2026-08-18 the Fourth Circuit affirmed a preliminary injunction covering several Quaker meetings, Sikh Temple Sacramento and Cooperative Baptist Fellowship congregations (Philadelphia Yearly Meeting v. DHS, No. 25-1512), while the District of Columbia court denied a similar request from Mennonite Church USA and other religious groups on 2025-04-11 for lack of standing, with an appeal pending (D.C. Cir. No. 25-5209). The Maryland district court had declined to extend the Quaker injunction nationwide, so the rescission is operative in general.

timeline.event: DHS issued a memorandum, signed by the Acting Secretary, that rescinds the 2021-10-27 guidelines on enforcement actions in or near protected areas and leaves officers to use discretion and common sense in place of bright-line rules; the ICE Director and CBP Commissioner may issue further guidance.

The District of Columbia district court denied a preliminary injunction sought by Mennonite Church USA and other religious groups, finding no showing of standing; the plaintiffs appealed (D.C. Cir. No. 25-5209).

The Fourth Circuit affirmed a preliminary injunction limiting enforcement at the plaintiffs' congregations, holding they were likely to succeed under the Religious Freedom Restoration Act; the district court had declined to make the injunction nationwide.
